content:
In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has put in more effort to fix bugs and improve performance. And among the beta versions so far, I think the most notable quality-of-life improvement is a fix for Messages when logging into a Mac.

When you log into a Mac running macOS Golden Gate, Messages should have already updated and finished syncing instantly.

One of the Mac's biggest selling points compared to a PC is how well it works together with the iPhone.

Continuity features like Universal Clipboard, iPhone Mirroring, and Handoff make operations between iPhone and Mac seamless.

However, macOS has long had one pain point that prevents a seamless continuity experience: shortly after logging in for the first time, Messages fails to stay in sync for a brief period.

You've probably all experienced this: after logging into a Mac, a flurry of Messages notifications pops up in the top-right corner, even though you've already read those messages long ago.

However, in macOS Golden Gate, Apple has listed performance and optimization as one of its priorities, significantly improving cross-device Messages syncing performance.

Apple says the syncing process is now more efficient—when your Mac comes online, the unread message count will be immediately more accurate, and you won't receive notifications for messages you've already read.

I mainly use my iPad Pro as my primary computer on a daily basis, with the Mac playing only a supporting role. Messages syncing between my iPhone and iPad has almost never had issues, so the Mac's consistently inferior experience has always bothered me.

With macOS Golden Gate, that annoyance is finally a thing of the past. From the beta's initial performance, Apple has indeed delivered.

How has Messages syncing been for you on the macOS Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.
